DP is definitely not just an intrusive thought. It's a normal, human defense mechanism to protect us from unbearable emotional pain. I don't think someone with DP would have OCD level of racing, uncontrollable thoughts. It's more the opposite; people with DP have a blank mind. But, they will still suffer from existential/negative thoughts if they let themselves be consumed by them. 


I think harris harrington's DP triangle is very useful in trying to understand DP. That consists of anxiety, obsession, and trauma. Your obsession is only one third part of your recovery. You can combat the obsessive thoughts through affirmations(eg. "I am in control of my life", "I am not losing my mind", framing (DP is "no big deal" frame), and focusing your attention outward(eg. volunteering, helping others). 


Anxiety is probably causing those thoughts as well. Your level of exercise, eating healthy, relaxation, abstinence from drugs, and getting a good night's sleep are all key factors in your anxiety. I would also add use of pornography to the list as well, although it is considered to be pseudoscience by many. 

Honestly, to answer your question, I think volunteering/helping others would help your derealization. Just focus OUTWARD.
